title: How Many Shots Does It Take? A Noise-Aware Quantum Resource Allocation Framework
authors: Prateek P. Kulkarni, Sumit K. Mandal
abstract: Any algorithm execution on quantum computers requires several repeated and costly executions (known as shots) to obtain reliable results. In this work, we propose a closed-form accurate analytical expression to determine optimal number of shots required for reliable execution of any algorithm on a quantum computer. We also present a theoretically grounded technique to distribute fixed shot budget across different partitions in a quantum circuit minimizing the total error. Our proposed analytical model helps to reduce the shots associated with reliable execution of quantum algorithms by about 58\% compared to current practice, in turn reducing the energy consumption by upto 62\%. Furthermore, our proposed optimal shot allocation technique across different partitions reduces total error by up to 73\% compared to conventional approaches.
summary: This paper introduces a comprehensive, noise-aware framework to optimize quantum algorithm execution on current hardware. It derives analytical methods to calculate the minimum necessary number of measurement shots and optimally distributes these shots across circuit partitions. The resulting resource allocation strategy significantly reduces both computational error and energy consumption compared to standard practices.
main_problem: The work addresses determining the optimal number of measurement shots required for reliable quantum algorithm execution and developing a noise-aware method to distribute a fixed shot budget across circuit partitions.
main_result: The proposed analytical framework reduces required shots by about 58% (leading to up to 62% energy reduction) and can reduce the total estimation error by up to 73% compared to conventional, non-optimized approaches.
method: It derives closed-form analytical expressions for optimal shot counts and uses Lagrange multipliers to solve a resource allocation problem that minimizes total estimation error subject to fixed budget constraints.
model_or_system: The analysis is applied to near-term quantum computers characterized by noise, limited gate fidelities, and the need for repeated circuit executions (shots). It models success probability using binomial/normal distributions incorporating hardware noise variance.
key_observables: Shots ($s$), Total Estimation Error ($\mathcal{E}$), Energy Consumption, Maximum Executable Depth ($d_{\max}$).
important_parameters: Coherence times ($T_1, T_2$), gate error probability ($p_g$), Circuit Depth ($d$), Target Success Probability ($P(s)$).
main_assumptions: Approximations are made for circuit execution time ($t_{circ} \approx d \cdot t_g$) and the noise variance calculation relies on suppressing higher-order terms in the noise model.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate comparisons of estimation error across different partitioning strategies, show the workflow for shot estimation and depth calculation, and compare energy consumption savings between optimal vs. equal shot allocation.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need for reliable shots to deriving analytical expressions for required shots, then developing a framework to calculate maximum feasible circuit depth ($d_{\max}$), and finally solving an optimization problem using Lagrange multipliers to optimally allocate shots across partitions to minimize total error.
why_interesting: While focused on computation, the rigorous mathematical treatment of noise accumulation and resource optimization (shot allocation) provides deep insights into the fundamental limits imposed by decoherence in open quantum systems, which is relevant for theoretical modeling of noisy physical platforms.
